correctness.rationale: The frozen fixed-point result survives, but its undirected Gibbs interpretation is not established: the printed array has a_1j=1 and a_j1=0 for j>1, whereas the cited correspondence in §5 starts with an undirected graph. Formal summability does not resolve this incompatibility. The repair removes the Gibbs/boundary-law count and specifies the operator explicitly. Since F_1=ell, division of the two positive mass equations gives r=(1+M_1)/(1+M_2), and M_2=(r−1)/(r^k−r); the recovered coordinates x_i=lambda_i M_p/L in parity p are positive and summable, so ordered mass roots and fixed points are in bijection. With A=(k−1)ell+k+1, six times the Taylor coefficient is 1−(k−1)^2−k^3+k[(k−1)^3 ell+(k+1)^3]/A; collecting terms gives the stated threshold. The large-s exponent is 2 with prefactor 1. The first dip and the divergence imply an interior global minimum and one crossing on either side for every level strictly between the minimum and L_c, with two swaps and a separate equal-mass root. The k=2 specialization matches the binary-tree algebra. Replay the repaired RESULT.md proof; the frozen script was inspected, not executed, and its recorded finite checks corroborate only the formal reduction. The revised claim does not require or assert any symmetric transfer kernel, equality of individual activities, or global count.
